summary: Gateway buffer pressure from long-polling sessions causing intermittent 5xx pulses
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-13 02:10 UTC, AcmeDocs observed intermittent 5xx spikes on several streaming endpoints. Errors manifest as HTTP 502/503 returned by the API Gateway and correlated runtime exits on a subset of ephemeral pods. Impact: Multiple customer processes experienced elevated error rates (~6-12% 5xx) for ~45 minutes; some streaming sessions were dropped mid-conversation. Environment: prod (us-east) - dedicated capacity pool allocated to AcmeDocs. Steps to reproduce: 1) Open >100 concurrent long-polling streaming sessions with keepalive interval ~30s. 2) Send periodic short messages (~20-50 chars) that keep sessions active for >20m. 3) Observe gateway and runtime metrics between 02:05-03:00 UTC. Observed behavior: - API Gateway accept queue and buffer growth (queue length metric spiking) - ingress-sidecar memory buffers increase and file descriptor counts approach soft limits - serving runtime threadpool saturation followed by worker exits (OOM-like memory pressure and SIGABRT on a few nodes) - elevated 502/503 rate at gateway, partial zero-byte responses on some streams Expected behavior: Gateway should shed or gracefully reject excess long-polling connections prior to upstream overload; streaming routes should not cause upstream runtime thread exhaustion. Logs/metrics: - Grafana: apigw.accept_queue_length spike, apigw.buffered_bytes rising - Traces show long-lived HTTP/2 streams with stalled WINDOW_UPDATE frames - Runtime logs: repeated "worker watchdog reset" and "prefetch lock contention" on 3 ephemeral nodes - No recent model rollouts for affected variant.
comments: Support (Maya): Escalated from CS after customer reported elevated 5xx and streaming drops at 02:20 UTC. Captured request ids and sample stream ids. Customer running ~160 concurrent streaming sessions at the time.

SRE (Liam): Noticed correlation with accept_queue_length and ingress buffer growth. Spun up additional ephemeral workers in the dedicated pool; initial scaling reduced but did not eliminate 5xx pulses.
Customer (AcmeDocs - engineer): We did not change client behavior; sessions are persistent as part of our sync feature. We can temporarily reduce concurrency if needed.
SRE (Liam): Added temporary rate limiter on streaming route for this tenant and increased keepalive idle timeout to force stale connection churn. Monitoring for next 30m.
Support (Maya): Customer confirmed partial improvement after throttling; still seeing low-rate 5xx spikes ~1-2%.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Long-lived HTTP/2 streams accumulate buffered data in the gateway/sidecar which increases file descriptor and memory pressure, delaying WINDOW_UPDATE and triggering upstream backlog and threadpool saturation.
Hypothesis 2: A recent edge config change (route consolidation last night) altered buffering behavior for low-throughput streams, increasing apigw write buffer thresholds.
Metrics examined: apigw.accept_queue_length, apigw.buffered_bytes, sidecar.fd_count, runtime.threadpool_queue_depth, runtime.watchdog_resets. All show correlated spikes during incidents.
Heap snapshots from two affected ephemeral pods show increased resident memory primarily in network buffers and per-connection state; no clear leak in model codepath.
No model kernel/quantization changes detected; no scheduled autoscaler changes in the same window except routine health probe adjustments.

Reproducibility: Synthetic reproduction with a loadtest that opens 180 long-poll streams with low message rate reproduced accept_queue growth and 5xx spikes in a staging cluster when edge buffer thresholds matched production config.
Related: linked ticket SUP-472901 contains similar accept-queue behavior on tenant warmup but differs in root cause (nvme/iowait).
fix_or_workaround: Immediate: Enabled tenant-level streaming rate limit (soft cap 120 concurrent streams) and increased keepalive interval to 90s for AcmeDocs; this reduced 5xx from ~8% to ~1-2%.
Triage: Rollback the edge route consolidation change to previous buffering parameters in a canary (10% traffic) to compare; release scheduled 2026-03-14 04:00 UTC.
Mitigation: Implement backpressure at apigw that signals clients with 429 when accept_queue_length > threshold rather than holding connections indefinitely.
Monitoring: Added alert rule for apigw.buffered_bytes > 75th percentile and runtime.watchdog_resets > 3/min for dedicated pools.
Customer workaround: AcmeDocs to stagger long-poll reconnection windows and reduce concurrency while we deploy fixes.
Note: Temporary throttling preserved customer SLA tier but will be revisited in follow-up postmortem.
next_steps: 1) Run canary rollback of route buffering params and monitor for 24h.
2) Engineering to add explicit WINDOW_UPDATE pacing and stronger backpressure in edge proxy (P0 engineering ticket to be created).
3) Update streaming route runbook to include accept_queue thresholds and tenant throttling guidance.
4) Schedule a post-incident review with AcmeDocs and platform teams (invite list: SRE, API Gateway, Ingress, Customer Success).
resolution_notes: In-progress: Temporary tenant throttling reduced customer impact. Canaries for edge config rollback scheduled. Final root cause pending canary comparison and deeper proxy WINDOW_UPDATE handling changes.
public_notes_for_customer: We observed gateway-side buffer growth from a combination of many long-lived low-throughput streaming sessions and a recent edge buffering parameter change. We applied tenant throttling to reduce load and scheduled a targeted canary rollback of buffering parameters while we implement a safer backpressure mechanism. We'll follow up after canary results and a post-incident review.
